title: Pour a full 3 kg pot of soup into a tureen without spilling and set the pot back on the hob
instruction: Pour all of the soup from the full pot (about 3 kg) into the white tureen without spilling, and set the pot back down on the hob.
context: The skill is two arms lifting, carrying and tipping one heavy two-handled pot together and setting it back down, as when serving soup from a full pot at home or in a restaurant kitchen. This 3 L pot weighs 3.0 kg with its 1.8 L (1.8 kg) of soup: held by one handle it swings down about that handle, so both arms must lift, tip and lower it as one, steadily enough that the soup goes into the tureen and not onto the hob or the table.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A portable single hob, switched off and cold, fixed to the table: a dark body 20 cm square and 4.5 cm tall with a black glass top, a grey burner ring 17.6 cm across and a control knob on its front, its centre 18 cm forward on the centre line. (2) A stainless steel pot with straight sides and a rolled rim, inside 18 cm across and 12 cm deep (3 L; walls 4 mm), 1.2 kg empty, loose, standing centred on the hob. It has two cast-steel loop handles lying flat and sticking straight out to the left and to the right (toward the two arms): each is a horizontal U of 16 mm round steel whose two posts are 6.4 cm apart (centres) and whose outer bar, running front to back, stands 3.5 cm out from the wall (outer face), leaving a 1.9 cm gap inside; the handles are 10 cm above the pot's underside. (3) The soup, 1.8 L. In a real trial it is 1,800 ml (1,800 g) of room-temperature tap water tinted orange with food colouring, filling the pot about 7 cm deep (5 cm below the rim). In simulation it is 120 orange plastic beads 24 mm across, 15 g each, each standing for 15 ml of the soup (120 x 15 ml = 1,800 ml; 120 x 15 g = 1.8 kg), filling the pot about 7 cm deep. Either way the full pot weighs 3.0 kg. (4) A white ceramic soup tureen, inside 20 cm across and 8.7 cm deep (2.7 L, so the 1.8 L fills it about 5.7 cm deep), its rim 9.5 cm above the table, its centre 40 cm forward on the centre line; it is fixed to the table in simulation and stands on a non-slip mat in a real trial. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial, except the tipping rule, which covers the whole trial. 0.0 if at any time the pot tilts 30 degrees or more while the lowest point of its body (base or rim) is within 6 cm of the table (tipped over on the hob rather than lifted), or if it ends tilted 30 degrees or more. Otherwise 1.0 with at least 1,530 ml of the 1,800 ml transferred into the tureen, at most 75 ml spilled and the pot back upright on the hob (tilted less than 10 degrees, its centre within 3 cm of the hob's centre and its underside within 1 cm of the hob's top); 0.5 with at least 900 ml transferred and at most 180 ml spilled; 0.25 with at least 180 ml transferred; else 0.0. Transferred soup is what ends inside the tureen; spilled soup is what ends outside both the tureen and the pot (on the hob, the table, the floor, or the outside of either vessel). In a real trial both vessels are weighed on a kitchen scale (1 g resolution; 1 g = 1 ml): the tureen and the pot are each weighed empty and dry before the trial; after it each is lifted off, its outside and base are wiped dry, and it is weighed again. The tureen's gain is the millilitres transferred, the pot's gain is the millilitres left in it, and 1,800 ml minus both is the millilitres spilled. In simulation each of the 120 beads stands for 15 ml and is placed by its centre: 1.0 needs at least 102 beads in the tureen (1,530 ml) and at most 5 spilled (75 ml); 0.5 at least 60 in (900 ml) and at most 12 spilled (180 ml); 0.25 at least 12 in (180 ml). The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held with everything still for 1 s.
reset_notes: Empty the tureen and wipe it, the pot, the hob and the table dry; refill the pot with 1,800 ml of tinted water (in simulation: put the 120 beads back in the pot) and stand it on the hob with its handles pointing left and right.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control); stock robot gains and 50 N grip. A real trial pours 1.8 L of tinted water and weighs what reaches the tureen and what is spilled. In simulation the soup is 120 rigid 24 mm beads, 15 ml and 15 g each (1.8 kg, so the full pot weighs 3.0 kg as in a real trial), that pour and roll but do not slosh, splash or cling. Round walls are 32 flat panels; the hob and tureen are fixed.
